title: Farewell to Miss Hussain, a beloved teacher
takeaway: A good teacher is a lamp. When they leave, the whole school feels it.
scene: Two poems for a teacher, Miss Hussain, who was leaving the Government Girls High School in Gojra. The first is a short Punjabi verse. The second is in Urdu, and the heading says the poet wrote it 'at the request of my daughter Tanveer-un-Nisa'. His daughter was one of Miss Hussain's students, and she asked her father to write a farewell poem.

original: جنہاں دی محنت دے صدقے سی قائم دیکھی ہریالی
علم ادب دے گلشن وچوں اوہ ٹر چلیا مالی
transliteration: Jinhaan di mehnat de sadqe si qaaim dekhi hariyaali
Ilm adab de gulshan vichon oh tur chaliya maali
translation: The one whose hard work kept everything green and growing,
that gardener is leaving the garden of learning.
couplets.story: Thanks to her hard work, the school was like a green, growing garden. Now the gardener herself is leaving.

original: پھکے پے گئے رنگ پھلاں دے غم کھا دا ہر ڈالی
احمدؔ دا دل اناں دی یادوں نئیں رہندا اجے خالی
transliteration: Phikke pe gaye rang phullaan de, gham khaanda har daali
Ahmad da dil inaan di yaadon nahin rehnda ajje khaali
translation: The flowers' colours have faded; every branch is grieving.
Ahmad's heart is not yet empty of memories of her.
couplets.story: With her leaving, the 'flowers', her students, look pale, and every branch seems sad. The poet still has his own memories of her.

original: وہ ماہ تاباں ملی جس سے ہمیں تابندگی
وہ شمع جس پائی علم و ادب کی روشنی
transliteration: Woh maah-e-taabaan mili jis se hamen taabindagi
Woh shamaa jis se paai ilm-o-adab ki roshni
translation: She was the shining moon who gave us our brightness,
the candle from which we received the light of knowledge and learning.
couplets.story: To her students she was like a bright moon that made them shine, and a candle that gave them the light of knowledge.

original: وہ ظرف جس سے بجھی تشنہ لبوں کی تشنگی
یہ ستم وہ آج ہم سے جدا ہو جائیں گی
transliteration: Woh zarf jis se bujhi tishna-labon ki tishnagi
Yeh sitam, woh aaj hum se juda ho jaayengi
translation: The vessel that quenched the thirst of thirsty lips:
how cruel, that today she will be parted from us.
couplets.story: She was like a jug of water for students who were thirsty to learn. It's hard to believe she's leaving today.

original: ان کے دم سے اس چمن میں رنگ و بو تھی نور تھا
غنچہ غنچہ اس ضیائے علم سے معمور تھا
transliteration: Un ke dam se is chaman mein rang-o-boo thi, noor tha
Ghuncha ghuncha is ziyaa-e-ilm se maamoor tha
translation: Because of her, this garden had colour, scent and light;
every bud was filled with the glow of learning.
couplets.story: She brought colour, fragrance and light to the school. Every student, every little bud, was full of the brightness of learning.

original: چہرہ چہرہ شادماں تھا کامراں مسرور تھا
وہ بہاریں اب کبھی ہم کو نظر نہ آئیں گی
transliteration: Chehra chehra shaadmaan tha, kaamraan, masroor tha
Woh bahaaren ab kabhi hum ko nazar na aayengi
translation: Every face was happy, successful and joyful;
we will never see those springs again.
couplets.story: Every student's face was happy and proud. Those happy days won't come back.

original: آپ کے لطف و عنایت کے وہ لمحے خوشگوار
دیر تک ان کے تصور میں رہیں گے سوگوار
transliteration: Aap ke lutf-o-inaayat ke woh lamhe khush-gawaar
Der tak un ke tasavvur mein rahenge sogawaar
translation: Those pleasant moments of your kindness and care,
we will grieve, thinking of them, for a long time.
couplets.story: They will remember her kindness for a long time, and miss it.

original: زیست کے ایوان میں جو بن گئی ہیں یادگار
ان حسین گھڑیوں کی یادیں ہر گھڑی تڑپائیں گی
transliteration: Zeest ke aiwaan mein jo ban gayi hain yaadgaar
Un haseen ghariyon ki yaaden har ghari tarpaayengi
translation: Those lovely moments that became monuments in the hall of life,
their memories will tug at us every moment.
couplets.story: The good times with her have become precious memories, and they'll make her students miss her every day.

original: اساتذہ سے آپ کی الفت رہے گی یادگار
کس طرح بھولیں گے ہم چاہت محبت اور پیار
transliteration: Asaatiza se aap ki ulfat rahegi yaadgaar
Kis tarah bhoolenge hum chaahat, mohabbat aur pyaar
translation: Your affection for the other teachers will be remembered.
How could we forget such warmth, love and care?
couplets.story: The other teachers will remember how kind she was to them too. How could anyone forget that much love?

original: آپ کی نظر کرم تھی باعث صد افتخار
وہ تبسم خیز کلیاں اب کہاں مسکائیں گی
transliteration: Aap ki nazar-e-karam thi baais-e-sad iftikhaar
Woh tabassum-khez kaliyaan ab kahaan muskaayengi
translation: Your kind glance was a reason for a hundred kinds of pride;
where will those smiling buds smile now?
couplets.story: One kind look from her made students proud. Without her, how will those smiling young students keep smiling?

original: یہ ستم ہے آج وہ ہم سے جدا ہو جائیں گی
transliteration: Yeh sitam hai aaj woh hum se juda ho jaayengi
translation: How cruel it is, that today she will be parted from us.
couplets.story: The poem ends by repeating the sad line: today she's leaving them.

why: It's a sweet, personal poem. A father wrote it because his daughter asked him to, to thank a teacher she loved. Anyone who has had a great teacher will understand it.
prompt: Which teacher made the biggest difference to you? What would you say to them?
notes: The first four lines are a Punjabi qita; the rest is an Urdu poem. The Urdu heading reads 'A poetic tribute of flowers, at the request of my daughter Tanveer', and below the poem: 'Flowers of devotion, presented to Miss Hassan/Hussain, Government Girls High School, Gojra'.
The Urdu stanzas repeat a refrain; here they are split into couplets for reading.
